about: The TypeScript counterparts of the Java API references of the guide Solving Graph Problems with Graphity (https://github.com/kaufco/graphity-doc), which links every name of the Java API to the API documentation of the language a reader picks. One entry per public or protected type, constructor and method of the four published Java modules, keyed by its declaration as java-refs.txt lists them: 'name' is the name in TypeScript, 'url' its page and anchor relative to the root of the API documentation (docRoot when built here, https://kaufco.github.io/graphity-ts/ when published), and 'note' what a reader of the Java text would not expect. Where TypeScript keeps Java's overloads as overload signatures of one name, 'signature' is the overload's signature as the API documentation shows it, without the return type and with type parameters by name only, so that the guide can tell the overloads apart where its Java text does; Java overloads that become one signature in TypeScript keep the plain name. Where TypeScript has no counterpart, 'name' and 'url' are null and 'reason' says why. test/apiMapping.test.ts checks the entries, and every url against the API documentation when it is built.
docCommand: npm run build && npm run docs

SortedIntView.listIterator(int).reason: JavaScript has no list iterator: its iterator protocol goes forward only. A SortedIntView is iterable from its start, with for...of, and get(index) reads any position.

SortedIntView.spliterator().reason: JavaScript has no spliterators and no streams to split for. A SortedIntView is iterable, and asInt32Array() gives its elements as an Int32Array without a copy.
